back: Any unwanted material produced by human activities.
Biodegradable: broken down by microorganisms (food, paper). Non-biodegradable: not broken down (plastics, glass, metals).

front: Examples of solid, liquid and gaseous waste
back: Solid: plastics, tins, tailings. Liquid: sewage, effluent, waste oil. Gaseous: smoke, CO, SO₂, methane.
Liquid waste (sewage or factory waste water) released into drains, rivers or the ground.
Tailings, cyanide solutions and mercury (from small-scale mining).

front: Wastes from soap making and tyre manufacture
back: Soap: waste oils and alkaline liquid. Tyres: rubber dust, off-cuts and fumes.
Dust and carbon dioxide (from heating limestone and burning fuel).
Observation and smell, pH tests, tests for ions (e.g. NaOH precipitates) and gases, collecting dust.
Reduce, reuse, recycle; separate; treat effluent; trap dust and gases; manage hazardous waste; laws and education.
Waste that is poisonous, corrosive, flammable or infectious, e.g. batteries, mercury, cyanide, medical waste.
